title: Finite coefficient descent of an affine perfect dg module
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S$ a finite type commutative $D$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $A$ a commutative $D$-algebra. Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme]. Use the standard coefficient resolutions $R_E$, the sheaf dg module categories, locally perfect objects, $U$, $\Phi_E$, $\widehat K$, and the normalized arrows $\nu_E$ of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization].

For every commutative $D$-algebra $E$, write $C_E=S\otimes_D R_E$ and let $D(C_E)$ be the localization of left dg modules at quasi-isomorphisms [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization, with the space a point]. Call an object perfect if it is a retract, in $D(C_E)$, of a dg module with a finite filtration whose quotients are finite sums of shifts of $C_E$. For every perfect $P\in D(C_A)$, there exist a commutative finite type $D$-algebra $E$, a factorization $D\to E\to A$, a perfect $P_E\in D(C_E)$, and an isomorphism
$$C_A\otimes_{C_E}^{\mathbf L}P_E\simeq P.$$
The scalar extension is the derived left-module extension of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization] on a point. No flatness or injectivity of the coefficient homomorphisms is assumed. Zero objects and zero coefficient rings are included.

source.place: Agent finite-coefficient descent refinement of Tag 09R3 (proposition-compact), using the functorial standard resolution of cotangent.tex Tag 08PM (definition-standard-resolution). Finite dg cells and their retract equations descend along the filtered union of finite type D-subalgebras; this exact coefficient-resolution formulation is not a separate assertion of those tags.

proof.text: If $A$ is finite type over $D$, take $E=A$ and $P_E=P$: extension along the identity dg algebra map is the identity, since ordinary tensor along the identity is naturally the identity and already descends to the localization. Suppose henceforth that $A$ is not finite type. Index by the finite type $D$-subalgebras $E_i\subseteq A$ which strictly contain the image of $D$. This is a nonempty directed set: adjoin one element outside the image to obtain an index, and the subalgebra generated by two finite generating sets is a common upper bound. Every element of $A$ belongs to such a subalgebra, by adjoining it to any one index. Thus their union is $A$. No $E_i$ has structure map an isomorphism from $D$, and $A\neq D$ as a $D$-algebra. Consequently none of the resolutions in this diagram uses the exceptional constant-resolution convention at $D$.

source.place: Finite type case and choice of directed coefficient diagram; agent elementary reduction.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-standard-normalized-resolution-filtered-colimit], $C_A=\varinjlim_i C_{E_i}$ as dg algebras, with homogeneous element lifting and eventual detection of finite differential equations. These are exactly the coefficient models of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization], since the diagram excludes its exceptional case. We may work with right modules over these graded-commutative dg algebras: a left module becomes a right module by $mb=(-1)^{|m||b|}bm$, and the same formula reverses this operation. For a degree-$r$ left graded map $f$, its signed linearity gives $f(mb)=f(m)b$ after this conversion. The Leibniz identity is preserved, as are homotopies, quasi-isomorphisms and shifts; the two signs on a shifted action cancel. For scalar extension the chain isomorphism $m\otimes b\mapsto(-1)^{|m||b|}b\otimes m$ identifies the right tensor with the left tensor. The sign formulas respect the balancing relation and the total differential, so they also identify their universal left derived functors. The existence of the right derived extension for the bimodule $C_{E_i}\to C_A$ is supplied by [lem-sfb-dg-bimodule-derived-adjunction].

source.place: Tags 09LS (lemma-derived-bc), 09LM (lemma-tensor); explicit graded-commutative left/right conversion and coefficient-colimit prerequisite.

proof.text: Choose the given retraction $P\xrightarrow{i}Q\xrightarrow{r}P$, $ri=1$, where $Q$ has a finite dg-cell filtration, and put $e=ir$ in $D(C_A)$. Choose homogeneous lifts $q_1,\ldots,q_t$ of the shifted units in successive filtration quotients, ordered by filtration. They form a graded free basis: each quotient is graded free, so lifting its basis gives a graded splitting, and induction through the finite filtration gives the assertion. Write $|q_a|=t_a$. Then $d_Qq_a=\sum_b q_b c_{ba}$, with $c_{ba}=0$ unless $q_b$ lies in an earlier filtration piece and $|c_{ba}|=t_a+1-t_b$. Extending the filtration constantly after its last term gives property (P). By [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-homotopically-projective] and [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived], $e$ is represented by a chain endomorphism $f:Q\to Q$, and $e^2=e$ supplies a degree-$-1$ graded right-linear $h$ with $f^2-f=d_Qh+hd_Q$. Write $f(q_a)=\sum_bq_bu_{ba}$ and $h(q_a)=\sum_bq_bv_{ba}$. All three arrays have finitely many entries. In particular no strict idempotence of $f$ has been assumed.

Lift the finitely many homogeneous entries $c_{ba},u_{ba},v_{ba}$ to one $C_{E_i}$. Keep the zero entries outside the earlier filtration pieces zero. On the graded free right module with generators $q_a$ in degrees $t_a$, define $d_i(q_a)=\sum_bq_bc_{ba,i}$ and extend by $d_i(q_ab)=d_i(q_a)b+(-1)^{t_a}q_ad(b)$. Define $f_i,h_i$ by the lifted arrays, with the same degrees as $f,h$. The equations $d_i^2(q_a)=0$, $(d_if_i-f_id_i)(q_a)=0$, and $(f_i^2-f_i-d_ih_i-h_id_i)(q_a)=0$ are finitely many equalities of homogeneous coefficients. Each is obtained by sums, products and differentials of the chosen entries, with signs fixed by the degrees. They hold in $C_A$ by step 3. The finite-equation clause of [lem-sfb-standard-normalized-resolution-filtered-colimit] makes them hold at one common later stage $E$. The Leibniz rule makes the first equality imply $d_E^2=0$ on the entire module, and graded linearity makes the other two equalities hold on the entire module. We have therefore constructed a finite-cell dg module $Q_E$, a chain map $f_E$, and a homotopy $f_E^2-f_E=d_Eh_E+h_Ed_E$. The filtration is by the same basis pieces; its quotients have zero generator differential and hence are sums of shifts of $C_E$. Its ordinary scalar extension, together with $f_E,h_E$, is the specified $Q,f,h$.

source.place: Agent finite homogeneous matrix argument using the coefficient-colimit prerequisite; compare Tag 09R3 (proposition-compact), finite-cell presentation.

proof.text: The class $e_E=[f_E]$ is idempotent in $D(C_E)$. This right-module derived category is triangulated by [lem-sfb-dg-derived-admissible-triangles] and has countable coproducts by [lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle]. Thus [lem-countable-coproducts-idempotent-complete] applies and gives a splitting $P_E\xrightarrow{i_E}Q_E\xrightarrow{r_E}P_E$ with $r_Ei_E=1$ and $i_Er_E=e_E$. Since $Q_E$ has the constructed finite-cell filtration, its retract $P_E$ is perfect by the definition in the item. The left/right conversion in step 2 makes this a perfect left dg object as required.

Apply $T=-\otimes_{C_E}^{\mathbf L}C_A$. It exists as a functor by [lem-sfb-dg-bimodule-derived-adjunction], so carries the displayed retraction equations to retraction equations. By [lem-sfb-dg-semifree-bimodule-tensor-computation], $T(Q_E)$ is canonically $Q_E\otimes_{C_E}C_A=Q$, and its naturality for $f_E$ identifies $T(e_E)$ with $[f]=e$. Thus $T(P_E)\xrightarrow{i'}Q\xrightarrow{r'}T(P_E)$ and $P\xrightarrow{i}Q\xrightarrow{r}P$ split the same idempotent. The maps $ri':T(P_E)\to P$ and $r'i:P\to T(P_E)$ are inverse: their composites are $r(i'r')i=rei=1_P$ and $r'(ir)i'=r'ei'=1_{T(P_E)}$. Convert back to left modules using step 2 to obtain $C_A\otimes_{C_E}^{\mathbf L}P_E\simeq P$. The structural map $D\to E$ and the inclusion $E\to A$ give the requested factorization. This construction needs no flatness of either map. Empty basis arrays give $P=0$; $A=0$ is already covered by the finite type case, and $S=0$ causes no exception to any equation.
